stem: When should preventive migraine medication be considered for an 11-year-old child?

options.text: Headaches are intense and last more than 48 hours
One mild headache settled after rest in a dark room
A single attack improved with paracetamol
The child prefers tablets to nasal spray
The parent would like to avoid discussing sleep or hydration

explanation: Headaches that are intense and last more than 48 hours are a scenario where preventive migraine medication may be considered in a child.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Headache

rationale: This is one of the explicit triggers for considering interval therapy rather than relying only on acute treatment.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because intense headaches lasting more than 48 hours match a criterion for considering preventive therapy.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a single mild headache that settles with rest does not meet the threshold for prophylaxis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because one attack that responds to paracetamol does not suggest a need for preventive medication.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because preference for one formulation over another is not an indication for prophylaxis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because avoiding lifestyle advice is not a reason to start preventive migraine medication.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
